fact_text: Depilex began in 1980 as a single salon in Karachi, opened by founder Masarrat Misbah, who said she has worked in the beauty business for over 45 years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: Depilex has grown from its first Karachi salon to more than 90 branches across Pakistan, and the founder said the brand has become a household name.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: The founder said Depilex was a competitor to most other salons in Pakistan during 1980 to 1990, when salon services began to extend from hair and makeup into wider grooming.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: In the 1980s neighbours and building owners treated beauty salons with suspicion, and the founder said the salon trade was not viewed favourably, so the founder had to build trust.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: In the 1980s Depilex offered fashion magazines free makeup for their model shoots in return for a credit, and the magazines then sent their models to the salon.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: The founder said salon businesses can be hurt when clients delay payment, and that regular non-payment is not workable for a small beauty business that must pay its staff.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: Depilex says its cosmetic line uses only halal ingredients, excluding animal fat and crushed-insect pigments, and it buys only from Shariah-compliant manufacturers and transport chains.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: Depilex says its training institute trains its own beauticians, and the founder said its certificates and diplomas are recognised abroad, with some courses offered through international collaborations.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: Depilex runs free training programmes for underprivileged women, with travel costs covered and donor funding from local and international agencies such as the ILO and UN programmes.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: Depilex salons are required to give work to two girls from their own area, according to the founder.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: Depilex has offered free treatment to women and girls disfigured by acid or burns for about 25 years, and trains those who wish to become beauticians.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: The founder said acid-burn survivors can need 30 to 40 operations, and some still do not look normal afterwards, which makes it hard to return them to work.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: The founder said most skin-treatment machines used in salons are imported, and their consumable products come with the machines, which makes such treatments expensive for clients.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: The founder warned that injectable treatments should be done only by specialists trained on that product, and said expensive machines placed in small towns have left clients with uneven lips and cheeks.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: The founder said skin-lightening treatments are harmful and should end, but demand for them has continued, which she described as a risk to customers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)

fact_text: The founder said she believes most television channel makeup rooms in Pakistan have used Depilex products over the ten years to 2026, and that its product range covers all needs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'From One Salon to 90+: Masarrat Misbah’s Depilex & Beauty Industry Story | Scaled | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-09-25)
